output.brief:
Don't approve the proposal. The rise is mainly a technical fault, not a nursing-performance problem.

On 12 August the alarm relay server moved to new hardware. The import silently skipped 11 of its 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips and repeat-alert suppression. Since then, phones in Pods A–C get about twice as many notifications per nurse (roughly 38 to over 80 per shift), acknowledgement times have doubled, and delayed-response incidents have risen about fourfold. Pod D, still on the old server, is unchanged. Agency, core and new-graduate nurses show the same rates, and Pod D has a similar agency share, so staffing mix doesn't explain it. Bedside alarm volume is flat and the monitor update came later.

I'm about 90% sure of this.

Next: have Clinical Engineering convert and re-import the rules (about four hours plus validation), with committee sign-off; hold Pod D's move until then; track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't switch off SpO2/technical forwarding; the central station is unstaffed at night. Separately check Room 14's silent-phone reports; the link to sick leave is unproven.
